explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/912 (Erdős–Selfridge): if n! = ∏ p_i^{k_i} then h(n) counts the distinct exponents k_i; prove there is c > 0 with h(n) ∼ c(n/log n)^{1/2}. In Lean h n is the cardinality of the range of nonzero values of (n!).factorization (the set of distinct exponents), and the statement is ∃ c > 0, (n ↦ h n) ~[atTop] (n ↦ c·(n/log n)^{1/2}). Faithful.
